HAVING completed the fourteen yean of exile, on the fifth day of 
the lunar fortnight, the elder brother of Lakshmana reached the 
hermitage of Bharadwaja and bowed low before that Ascetic. 
Paying obeisance to him, he enquired of the Sage, saying:-
" 0 Blesaed One, dost thou mow if all are well and happy in 
the city ? Is Bharata fixed in his duty ? Do my mothers still 
live?" 
Thus did Rama question Bharadwaja and that great Sage, 
smiling, answered the Prince of the Raghus cheerfully and 
said:-

brief.summary_1line: After exile, Rama meets sage Bharadwaja, learns Bharata faithfully rules in his name, and asks a boon that fruit trees flourish along his road to Ayodhya.

image_candidates.scene_text: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana bow before the radiant sage Bharadwaja in his forest hermitage as ascetics look on.
Bharadwaja recounts Rama’s entire saga with calm certainty, seated in meditation as the prince listens respectfully.
Rama requests that every tree along the road to Ayodhya bear fragrant, honeyed fruit though it is not the season.
